0.1 This Indian

FOREWORD

Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 August 1978, after the draft finalized by the Sectional Committee had been Automobile Electrical Equipment approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first published in 1969. This revision has been undertaken to upgrade requirements and bring in line with international practice. 0.3 The oil pressure switch is intended to give warning of the low pressure of the oil through an indicating lamp in the dashboard. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with The number of significant places retained in the rounded IS : 2-1960*. off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This
ments

standard covers the basic mechanical and electrical requireand methods of test for 6, 12 and 24 V hydraulically operated oil pressure switches for use in automobiles. These switches shall operate as the pressure of oil decreases.

2.2 Rated Current - The value of the current specified by manufacturer at which the switch is designed to operate satisfactorily.

2.3 Type Tests - Tests carried out to prove conformity with the specification. These are intended to prove the general qualities and design of a given type of oil pressure switch. 2.4 Routine Tests - Tests carried out on each oil pressure check requirements which are likely to vary during production. 2.5 Acceptance Tests - Tests carried for the purpose of acceptance of the lot. 3. MATERIAL, CONSTRUCTION out on samples taken switch to

from a lot

AND

WORKMANSHIP

3.1 Material - The body of the switch shall be made of material suitable No hygroscopic material shall be used unless they have for tropical use. been previously rendered moisture-proof. 3.2 Construction - The switches shall be so designed and constructed as to be mechanically robust and free from any operational hazards. They shall be constructed so as to be capable of withstanding vibration, shocks, etc, met with in normal use. They should have adequate resistance to heat and cold. The diaphragm fitted inside the switch shall be capable of withstanding oil at temperature between - 25" and 120�C for 70 hours. All exposed metallic surfaces likely to be affected by atmospheric conditions shall be adequately protected to prevent corrosion. The maximum tightening torque for dry sealing should be 30 N.m. 3.3 Workmanship - All parts with good engineering practice. 4. 6.0.4 In case of failure of one or more samples in type tests, the testing authority may call for fresh samples not exceeding twice the number of original samples and subject them to the test(s) in which failure occurred. 1-A load and with contacts closed, the 6.4 mV Drop Test - With voltage drop due to contact resistance shall not exceed 150 mV before endurance test and 400 mV after endurance test. 6.4.1 For switches with normally open contacts, the mV drop test shall be carried out at maximum operating pressure given in 6.3. 6.5 Endurance Test - The switch shall be tested for 100000 cycles of operation at the rated voltage and a current of 0.4 A. The test shall be carried out using SAE 40 oil maintained at a temperature of 100 + 5�C. The oil pressure shall be varied between the limits of 0 and 500 kPa in 0.1 to 0'5 second. The pressure shall be maintained constant at either limit for l:O to 2.0 seconds. At the end of this test, the switch shall pass the performance test ( 6.3 ) and mV drop test ( 6.4 ) satisfactorily. 6.6 Pressure Test - The switch shall be subjected to a hydraulic pressure of 1 500 kPa for 2 minutes with SAE 40 oil at 100 -+ 5�C and there shall be no leakage. There shall be no change in the operating range of the switch after this test. 6.7 Test for Salt
